{{Short description|German chemist}}
'''Tanja Weil''' is a German chemist known for her research for in [[Macromolecule|macromolecular]] chemistry, [[dendrimer]]s, [[dye]]s, [[protein]], and [[peptide]]s. As of 2025, Weil holds the position of director at the [[Max Planck Institute for Polymer Research]].

== Education ==
Weil conducted her undergraduate in chemistry at the [[Technical University of Braunschweig]] in Germany from 1993 until 1998. She then moved to the [[University of Bordeaux 1|University of Bordeaux I]] in France from 1993 to 1998. She did her Ph.D. under the mentorship of [[Klaus Müllen]] at the [[Max Planck Institute for Polymer Research]] from 1998 to 2002.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Director |url=https://www.mpip-mainz.mpg.de/en/weil/director |access-date=2024-03-22 |website=Max Planck Institute for Polymer Research |language=en}}</ref>

== Career ==
From 2002–2008 Weil was the director of Chemical Research and Development at Merz Pharmaceuticals GmbH in Frankfurt. In 2008, she joined the [[National University of Singapore]] as an associate professor. She then worked at [[Ulm University]] from 2010 to 2016. In 2017 she moved to the Max Planck Institute for Polymer Research where she heads the division of Synthesis of Macromolecules.<ref name=":0" />

== Research ==
Weil is known for her work on the synthesis and development of macromolecules with precise structural characteristics and versatile functionalities. The press has covered her research include her 2024 work that described a material that separates chemical compounds with similar sizes, but varying chemical properties,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Corner |first=Lexie |date=2024-09-26 |title=Nanometer-Scale Sieve Separates Ions with Precision |url=https://www.azonano.com/news.aspx?newsID=41073 |access-date=2025-01-04 |website=AZoNano |language=en}}</ref> and her 2023 research that used fibers similar viruses to introduce DNA into cells.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schneider |first=Christian |date=August 23, 2023 |title=Learning from viruses: Molecular fibers can help to introduce genetic material into cells |url=https://phys.org/news/2023-08-viruses-molecular-fibers-genetic-material.html |access-date=2025-01-04 |website=phys.org |language=en}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
In 2002 she received the [[Otto Hahn Medal]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Weil, Tanja |url=https://www.mpg.de/10429526/polymer-research-weil |access-date=2025-01-04 |website=www.mpg.de |language=en}}</ref> In 2014 she gave the Bruno-Werdelmann lecture.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Werdelmann-Stiftung {{!}} Deutsches Stiftungszentrum |url=https://www.deutsches-stiftungszentrum.de/stiftungen/professor-werdelmann-stiftung |access-date=2025-01-04 |website=www.deutsches-stiftungszentrum.de |language=de}}</ref> Weil received the Netherlands Scholar Award for Supramolecular Chemistry in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Netherlands Award for Supramolecular Chemistry – FMS Research Center |url=https://fmsresearch.nl/netherlands-award-for-supramolecular-chemistry/ |access-date=2025-01-04 |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2023 Weil received the [[Karl Ziegler]] award.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Karl Ziegler Foundation {{!}} Gesellschaft Deutscher Chemiker e.V. |url=https://en.gdch.de/gdch/foundations/karl-ziegler-foundation.html |access-date=2025-01-04 |website=en.gdch.de |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Goedecke |first=Catharina |date=2023-04-25 |title=Karl Ziegler Prize for Tanja Weil |url=https://www.chemistryviews.org/karl-ziegler-prize-for-tanja-weil/ |access-date=2024-03-22 |website=ChemistryViews |language=en-US}}</ref>
